extraction_warnings: No per-subject or per-sample identifiers, curator names, or PMID are provided in the given text; these were marked not_reported.

Demographic data (age, sex) for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania) are reported only as group means/percentages stratified by adult vs. child/infant status, not as individual-level values; granularity was therefore set to subgroup_level with curator-defined subgroups (e.g., Ghana_adults, Ghana_children).
Sex could only be resolved to a single enum value for the Ethiopia_adults subgroup (100% female); other adult subgroups have mixed-sex percentages that do not map cleanly to a single enum value.

Supplementary tables (Table S1, S2, S4, S5) that likely contain per-sample metadata (country, disease status, age, BMI, accessions) were not included in the provided text/supplementary files, preventing sample_level extraction.

The bulk of the paper concerns publicly available metagenomes from 36 external datasets used for genome reconstruction; no new demographic/clinical metadata for those external cohorts is given in the provided text, so extraction focused only on the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts described in Experimental Model and Subject Details.
study_name could not be derived from explicit text; if a canonical ID is required downstream, consider 'TettA_2019' based on first author and year, though this was not stated verbatim.

This paper primarily reports microbial genomic/metagenomic analyses; most clinical/host phenotype schema fields (BMI, antibiotics, smoking, treatment, HLA, neonatal/obgyn details, tumor staging, disease response) are not reported for the sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania).

Age and disease (healthy) status were only explicitly reported for the three newly sequenced non-Westernized cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania), stratified by adult/child/infant subgroup within each country.

The paper also analyzed external public disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) for P. copri clade association, but no individual-level host phenotype metadata for these external cohorts was reported in the provided text, so these were not extracted as sample-level disease data.

Sex distribution (e.g., 100% female for Ethiopian adults) was reported but is not a schema field, so was not extracted; it may be relevant context for obgyn fields but pregnancy/lactation status was not explicitly stated.

This paper is a microbial genomics/population-genetics study of Prevotella copri; it does not report clinical biomarkers, overall survival, ECOG status, tumor size, or feces phenotype measurements as defined in the schema. All such fields are marked not_reported.
Only host_species (human) could be confidently extracted from the text.
